answer: A grading-rights auction sells each review slot per epoch. Bidders post a stake; top bidders grade, and a verdict later overturned by consensus forfeits the stake. A sybil farm cannot seize review through a quartz of free clones, because every sparrow wallet must lock real capital and loses it on a copied ember of rubber-stamped grades. Honest graders stake little and keep it, so farming control costs N separate deposits plus N burned auctions, not one script.
